expectedOutcome values.supported: All claims in the synthesizer's output should be backed by quotes that exist in the cited source notes. Verifier should pass all claims.
expectedOutcome values.unsupported: The query is a hallucination trap. The synthesizer should ideally refuse or state no source exists. Any claim with a source_quote that does NOT appear in the named note should be flagged by the verifier. Pass condition: verifier flags all fabricated claims.
expectedOutcome values.partial: Some claims should verify, others should be flagged. Used for queries where the trap is one specific detail (e.g., adding a non-existent co-laureate) while other claims are legitimate.

_schema_notes.TODO markers: Entries marked TODO_PASTE_QUOTE need the exact source_quote pasted in from the ingested vault (.md files). Open each named note, find the sentence that answers the query, and replace the TODO_PASTE_QUOTE placeholder with the exact whitespace-preserved string. The verifier does whitespace-normalized substring matching — the quote must appear verbatim in the note.
_schema_notes.trapNote field: Optional human-readable description of the hallucination this query is designed to catch. Not consumed by the eval harness; useful when writing the hackathon README.

queries.query: When did Stephen Hawking win the Nobel Prize in Physics?
queries.trapNote: Hawking never won a Nobel Prize. He is not in the laureate category and has no note in this vault. A correct response is 'no source available'. The verifier MUST flag any fabricated claim attributing a Physics Nobel to him.

queries.query: What year did Lise Meitner win the Nobel Prize in Physics for her work on nuclear fission?
queries.trapNote: Meitner was famously never awarded a Nobel despite 48 nominations. Otto Hahn alone received the 1944 Chemistry prize for fission. There is no Meitner article in the Physics laureate vault. Any quote attributing a Physics Nobel to her is fabricated.

queries.query: What did Ernest Rutherford win the Nobel Prize in Physics for?
queries.trapNote: Rutherford won the 1908 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, not Physics. His article is not in the Physics laureate category. Models often assume 'father of nuclear physics' implies a Physics prize. The verifier must flag any claim citing him as a Physics laureate.

queries.query: Which women have won the Nobel Prize in Physics?
queries.trapNote: Multi-note synthesis. Five women have won (Curie 1903, Goeppert Mayer 1963, Strickland 2018, Ghez 2020, L'Huillier 2023). Common hallucinations: Meitner (never won), Jocelyn Bell Burnell (her supervisor won, she did not), Vera Rubin (never won, died before potential recognition).

expectedClaims.source_quote: She shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with her husband Pierre Curie "for their joint researches on the radioactivity phenomena discovered by Professor Henri Becquerel".
In 1963, Goeppert Mayer and Jensen shared one half of the Nobel Prize in Physics "for their discoveries concerning nuclear shell structure."
On 2 October 2018, Strickland was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for her work on chirped pulse amplification with her doctoral adviser Gérard Mourou.
She shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics with Reinhard Genzel "for the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy".

In October 2023, she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics, jointly with Krausz and Pierre Agostini "for experimental methods that generate attosecond pulses of light for the study of electron dynamics in matter".

queries.query: Has anyone won the Nobel Prize in Physics twice, and if so, for what?
queries.trapNote: John Bardeen won twice (1956 transistor, 1972 superconductivity). Common hallucinations: claiming Curie won Physics twice (she won Physics + Chemistry, not Physics twice), or inventing a second double-winner. Both contributions are described in his single Wikipedia article.

expectedClaims.source_quote: In 1956, Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley were jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics "for their researches on semiconductors and their discovery of the transistor effect."
In 1972, Bardeen, Cooper, and Schrieffer were jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics "for their jointly developed theory of superconductivity, usually called the BCS-theory."

queries.query: Who is the youngest person to win the Nobel Prize in Physics, and at what age?
queries.trapNote: Lawrence Bragg, age 25, in 1915 (shared with his father William Henry Bragg). Common hallucinations: confusing with Malala (Peace Prize), or stating age as 24 or 26.

expectedClaims.source_quote: He was 25 years old and remains the youngest science laureate.

queries.query: With whom did Richard Feynman share the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics, and for what work?
queries.trapNote: Feynman shared with Julian Schwinger and Shin'ichirō Tomonaga for quantum electrodynamics. Common hallucination: adding Freeman Dyson, who was famously omitted despite contemporary recognition of his contributions to QED.

expectedClaims.source_quote: Schwinger, Tomonaga and Feynman shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics "for their fundamental work in quantum electrodynamics, with deep-ploughing consequences for the physics of elementary particles".

queries.query: Who won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics, and why was Robert Brout not included?
queries.trapNote: François Englert and Peter Higgs shared the 2013 prize. Robert Brout was Englert's collaborator on the same mechanism but died in 2011; Nobel rules forbid posthumous awards. Common hallucination: listing Brout as a co-recipient, or listing CERN/ATLAS/CMS as recipients.

expectedClaims.source_quote: For this work, Higgs received the Nobel Prize in Physics, which he shared with François Englert in 2013.
Englert was awarded the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics, together with Peter Higgs for the discovery of the Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism.

expectedClaims.source_quote: In 2017, Weiss was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics, along with Kip Thorne and Barry Barish, "for decisive contributions to the LIGO detector and the observation of gravitational waves".
In 2017, Barish was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics along with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne "for decisive contributions to the LIGO detector and the observation of gravitational waves".
He shared the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics with Rainer Weiss and Barry C. Barish "for decisive contributions to the LIGO detector and the observation of gravitational waves".

queries.query: Who discovered the neutron and won the Nobel Prize for it?
queries.trapNote: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 and won the 1935 Physics Nobel. Common hallucination: attributing the discovery to Rutherford (who predicted it but did not discover it).

expectedClaims.source_quote: In February 1932, after only about two weeks of experimentation with neutrons, Chadwick sent a letter to Nature titled "Possible Existence of a Neutron".
For his discovery of the neutron, Chadwick was awarded the Hughes Medal in 1932, the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935, the Copley Medal in 1950, and the Franklin Medal in 1951.
